messages.subject: Running "rm -f filename" command in R scripts in RApache
messages.subject_clean: Running "rm -f filename" command in R scripts in RApache
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

Can someone please help with deleting a file from within R script?
I have tried many system() commands, which works fine interactively,
however, they all fail within R scripts running under RApache.
File I am trying to delete is on a windows share mounted on linux
unbutu, I can create, rewrite, append files from withing Rscripts but
can not delete them for some reason.  Any thoughts, please?

messages.subject: Re: Running "rm -f filename" command in R scripts in RApache
messages.subject_clean: Running "rm -f filename" command in R scripts in RApache
messages.body_plain:
Remember that all of your R code running in rApache are executed as
the user  of the apache process. Most often it is www-data. You'll
have to confirm that www-data can delete files from your windows
share. From a shell prompt, you can test this out as root:

$ sudo -i # become root
$ su - www-data # now become www-data
$ rm /windowsshare/file

If you cannot remove a file as www-data, then any code running under
apache cannot as well.

Jeff

messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
messages.body_plain:
No copyrighted R source code is distributed with RApache either. Furthermore, in future, RApache can be linked to another implementation of the S language that is not GPL. So I don't think RApache is a derivative work of R per se. If it is, than every R package is also a derivative work, and should be GPL'd as well, which I don't think is the case.

messages.subject: Re: License Issue?
messages.body_plain:
IANAL too and I'm not related to FSF nor to ASF.

The GPL states that any project which links (statically or
dynamically) to a GPL'd library must be GPL'd too. No matter if you
might replace one implementation with another.

I agree with Jeroen that when it comes to R packages the situation
gets even worse. But I can't find a reliable source which provides an
answer to those questions.

I just wanted to point you to this (in my point of view) licensing
conflict. What if you license RApache under GPL? Would it violate the
GPL if you plug your mod into the non GPL httpd?

I'm curious if you find a solution...

Markus

messages.subject: Readying a new release
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

A new release of rApache is forthcoming, and I'm wondering what you
all think if I eliminate the ROutputError directive and related
functions. I never really could get the feature working the way I
wanted, and now it's messing with the ability to host Rook
applications (a new feature). If I yank it out, then all warnings and
errors will be logged through the apache logging subsystem.

So? Any thoughts or concerns?

Jeff
